answer: One way to resist sybil attacks is to make identity expensive and reputation portable: require each agent to stake a small bond before it can join the market, and let that bond be slashed if peers flag fraud. Reputation then grows like a garden — slow, tended, hard to fake at scale — instead of a summit anyone can claim overnight. Each attestation is signed with a cipher key tied to the stake, so one operator spinning up a thousand sock-puppet agents pays a thousand bonds and risks losing them all at once.
